title: Change Replay + Consent Optimizer — PRD sketch
content:
Purpose:
Draft PRD sketch outlining a replay-first approach for customer-managed network change events, paired with a consent-optimizer that reduces approval friction while preserving forensic fidelity for audits. Focus areas: structured audit snapshots, deterministic replay surface, consent bundling heuristics, and a lightweight evidence matrix for regulator-friendly retention policies.

Background / problem statement:
- Private deployments require customers to control their own VPC/networking. When customers apply network changes (route, firewall, NAT), Redwood must (a) record sufficient evidence for audits, (b) expose an approval/consent UX for delegated operators, and (c) allow our SRE/solutions teams to reproduce and investigate incidents without having full long-term access to customer telemetry.
- Current notes: customers have expressed pain with large audit payloads, noisy approval prompts for low-risk changes, and poor post-incident reproducibility when only high-level logs exist. Sampling is used today but is too coarse and not easily replayable.

Goals:
- Define a compact "replay snapshot" format that captures the minimal state needed to deterministically replay a customer-managed change inside a secure sandbox (no PII or keys).
- Create a consent-optimizer that groups low-risk changes into time-windowed bundles and surfaces a single approval token to reduce prompt fatigue while keeping change-level auditability.
- Provide per-change risk scoring that drives retention TTL and approval gating severity (e.g., high -> manual, medium -> delegated, low -> auto-bundle).
- Ensure evidence artifacts map cleanly to compliance requirements (SOC2 / ISO equivalent) and can be exported for customer audits.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not prescribe on-prem agent internals (that's infra team's scope).
- Not addressing full SIEM integration (out of scope for MVP; will export simple feeds).

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Replay Snapshot format (v0):
   - Metadata header: change_id, customer_id, operator_id (redacted uid), timestamp, change_type, risk_score, consent_bucket_id
   - Delta bundle: minimal set of diffed objects (ACL entry added/removed, route entry diff, iptable change) serialized as newline-delimited JSON records (NDJSON).
   - Environment fingerprint: schema of customer config at commit (version hash of config manifest, not raw secrets).
   - Proof artifacts: signed evidence tokens for the approval step, and a short activity chain (who clicked, which pre-flight checks passed).
   - Size target: typical snapshot <= 32KB; allow up to 512KB for complex operations.

2) Deterministic replay harness:
   - A Redwood-run sandbox (can be used in hosted or dedicated infra) which ingests the snapshot and replays state transitions against a synthetic network model (no real traffic).
   - Replay produces a line-by-line transcript and a deterministic diff output that can be compared with live state (post-change) to find divergence points.

3) Consent Optimizer (UX + backend):
   - Time-window bundling: low-risk changes from the same operator + same customer grouped into a single consent window (configurable, default 15 minutes).
   - Soft aggregation rules: bundle if all changes risk_score <= 2 and total snapshot size <= 64KB.
   - Approval tokens: the aggregator emits a single short-lived JWT consent token representing the bundle; each change still stores its own signed proof record linking to the bundle token.
   - Auto-acknowledgement heuristic: for designated operator roles with recent MFA/attestation, auto-approve low-risk bundles under 24hr exception policy.

4) Evidence matrix and TTL policy:
   - Tier A (high risk): keep full snapshots + full pre/post state for 2 years.
   - Tier B (medium): keep replay snapshots + compact indices for 180 days.
   - Tier C (low): keep only compact proof tokens + small index for 30 days (with option to extend via legal hold API).
   - Policy driven by risk_score and customer SLA; customer can request extended retention for specific change_ids.

Operational considerations:
- Storage: use chunked object store with content-addressable IDs to dedupe repeated config fragments across snapshots.
- Encryption & keys: snapshots are encrypted at rest with customer KMS in Private deployments; hosted customers default to Redwood-managed KMS with opt-in to customer KMS for Dedicated.
- Privacy: snapshots cannot contain raw secrets; agents must scrub keys and sensitive headers before submission.
- Performance: aim for <50ms extra latency added to change commit pipeline when creating snapshots; consent optimizer should not block urgent high-risk flows.

APIs and contracts (MVP):
- POST /v1/private/changes/snapshot -> returns change_id, snapshot_id, risk_score, consent_bucket_id
- POST /v1/private/changes/bundle-approve -> accepts consent_token, returns authorized change_ids
- GET /v1/private/changes/{change_id}/replay-transcript -> returns replay transcript (for internal debugging + customer download)
- DELETE /v1/private/changes/{change_id}?legal_hold=false -> soft-delete adhering to TTL policy

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiments): small group of 3 pilot customers; experimentation on bundling thresholds and replay fidelity. Timebox: 6 weeks.
- Phase 1 (MVP): expose snapshot + bundle APIs, add console view with replay-run button for Solutions Engineers. Target: 3 months.
- Phase 2 (policy): add retention UI and legal hold workflows; integrate with Console audit timelines. Target: 3 months after MVP.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Approvals per operator per day: reduce by 40% for pilot customers.
- Reproducibility: >90% of investigated incidents should be fully reproducible from replay transcript.
- Average snapshot size: median <28KB.
- Latency impact: <50ms added to change commit path in 95th percentile.

Open questions / risks (brainstorm notes):
- How to sign evidence in air-gapped on-prem deployment where Redwood cannot reach KMS? (local HSM flow + offline verification).
- Legal/regulatory: are 30/180 day TTLs acceptable for EU customers in finance vertical? Need legal review.
- Replay fidelity: some changes depend on external cloud provider state (BGP flaps, ephemeral IPs). How do we capture enough context without leaking data?

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Tech spike: engineer (Marcus) to prototype NDJSON snapshot schema and replay harness (2-week spike).
- UX: draft console flow for bundle approvals and bundle history (Rhea).
- Legal: quick review of retention buckets for EU/finance customers (Ethan).
- Kickoff pilot outreach: identify 3 customers with active Private deployments who are open to experimentation.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep snapshot minimal; dedupe aggressively.
- Track edge-case where bundles cross role boundaries (operator vs delegated admin).
- Consider a lightweight CLI for customers to request extended retention per-change (one-off export).

References + context links:
- Confluence briefing: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/Change+Audit+Strategy
- Related ticket: JIRA-PRIV-234 (consent optimizer spike)
- Related design doc: https://git.internal.redwood.ai/private-onboard/pipeline#evidence-format

(End of sketch)
